facts.text: ScilaWrapper is the SCILA device wrapper; it extends DeviceWrapper and registers a status event
The wrapper loads the vendor IHC_PMS_Lib.Scila assembly through pythonnet
GetTemperature returns the current temperature, the target temperature and the temperature-control flag
SetTemperature takes a target temperature and a temperature-control flag and passes a None target through as None
GetAutoBoostCo2 returns the auto-boost flag and the boost-state string
SetAutoBoostCo2 writes the CO2 auto-boost flag
GetCo2FlowStatus returns the CO2 flow status string
SetCo2NormalFlow writes the normal CO2 flow flag
GetDoorStatus returns the four drawer status strings
GetValveStatus returns the Gas_Boost, Gas_Normal and H2O valve status strings
GetStatus returns a StatusWrapper whose State and Locked properties are the SiLA state and the lock flag
GetDeviceIdentification returns a DeviceIdentificationWrapper with the device name, firmware version, manufacturer and serial number
Abort is a mandatory SiLA command on DeviceWrapper
The example application sets the SCILA temperature to 37 and enables control, and reads the current temperature, target temperature and control flag
The example application enables the CO2 auto boost and the normal CO2 flow and reads their statuses
The example configuration enables the SCILA wrapper
The clone states no temperature unit and no numeric temperature range; the example method set gives 27 and 110 without a unit
The vendor libraries require .NET Framework 4.8 or Mono and are not publicly downloadable
